headline: Giza (Pyramids) served as secondary necropolis before Khufu's pyramid
summary: Giza (Pyramids) served as secondary necropolis before Khufu's pyramid. Conservatively dated to late 3rd dynasty or early 4th dynasty during Khufu's reign Could be even older with little excavation and analysis undertaken Risner believed Giza (Pyramids) was occupied and used as a necropolis before Khufu
post_text: Researchers conservatively date the Wadi Cemetery to the late 3rd or early 4th dynasty, though it could be older with little analysis undertaken. Some scholars believed Giza was occupied as a necropolis before Khufu. Before rising to prominence, Giza held secondary status to Saqqara, Maidum, and Dashur. The Western Cemetery and Wadi Cemetery add to growing evidence of pre-Khufu archaeology at Giza. Research by Mark Lehner and Zahi Hawass also suggests a pre-Khufu settlement existed there.

headline: Academia uses biased dating methods influenced by Bible
summary: Academia uses biased dating methods influenced by Bible. The 'DiCaprio dating' system confuses minimum with maximum dates Archaeologists date to the youngest spectrum possible 19th century scholars pushed a 6,000-year date based on Bible calculations
post_text: Some researchers argue archaeological dating methods have problems — Göbekli Tepe was dated to the Pre-Pottery Neolithic (c. 9500–8000 BCE) using radiocarbon dating, which confirmed earlier suspicions of its great age. The debate over dating methodologies continues within the field.

headline: Precision stone vases as modern fakes? Host argues cost, tooling and provenance say no
summary: Precision stone vases as modern fakes? Host argues cost, tooling and provenance say no. Making the vases as they are today would take five-axis CNC machines grinding granite, at very high cost Plain stone vases were worth little on the 1960s to 1980s antiquities market, so such costly forgery would not pay A forger working for profit could have turned out imprecise copies from an ordinary lathe shop, and nobody was doing precision metrology on the vases until recently
post_text: The host argues that calling these precision stone vases modern forgeries makes little sense. Reproducing them today would take five-axis CNC machines grinding granite at great cost, while plain stone vases were worth little on the 1960s to 1980s antiquities market. A forger after profit could have turned out imprecise copies on a lathe. Even the least documented vases have histories back to the 1980s or the 1960s, before computer-controlled five-axis mills, and the lug-handled forms have geometry a lathe alone cannot produce.

A forger working for profit could have turned out imprecise copies from an ordinary lathe shop, and nobody was doing precision metrology on the vases until recently

headline: Geologists debate natural volcanic formation vs man-made structure
summary: Geologists debate natural volcanic formation vs man-made structure. Discussion centers on whether the formation is natural or constructed One hypothesis is that it could be a volcanic dyke Comparison made to megalithic structures observed in Peru
post_text:
The Natural Wall remains a mystery. One side looks like a volcanic dyke, but the block-like appearance on the other side resembles megalithic structures found in Peru. Some blocks even have rolled edges like placed stones. Locals weigh in on the debate 🗿

Note: The formation is officially called the 'Natural Wall' and is described by geologists as a resistant vertical bed of Jacobsville Sandstone, not a volcanic dyke. The volcanic dyke hypothesis is one proposed by non-expert observers to explain its appearance.

headline: Belovode furnaces: earliest secure copper smelting evidence worldwide, dated to 4900 BC
summary: Belovode furnaces: earliest secure copper smelting evidence worldwide, dated to 4900 BC. Excavations at Belovode and Pločnik led by archaeometallurgist Miljana Radivojević uncovered copper slag, malachite beads, and metal droplets in Vinča-period contexts Results confirmed through chemical and microstructural analysis, published in a 2021 monograph Pushed back confirmed date of true copper smelting to 4900 BC, making Belovode the earliest secure evidence of extractive metallurgy anywhere in the world
post_text: Archaeometallurgist Miljana Radivojević's excavations at Belovode and Pločnik uncovered copper slag, malachite beads, and metal droplets in Vinča-period layers, confirmed by chemical and microstructural analysis published in a 2010 Journal of Archaeological Science paper. This pushes confirmed copper smelting to c. 5000 BC, making Belovode the earliest secure evidence of extractive metallurgy in Europe. Rudna Glava is one of the earliest known copper mines, mined at scale. Incredible! 🔥⚒️

headline: China's Dawenkou holds oldest elongated skulls claimed at 10,000 years old
summary: China's Dawenkou holds oldest elongated skulls claimed at 10,000 years old. Host claims Dàrén Cùyū (Darren Cuyu) in China contains the oldest known elongated skulls, dated to approximately 10,000 years ago Host notes the site's top level was excavated first, meaning all archaeologists have passed through the oldest strata Host criticizes archaeological methodology of finding later-period artifacts in lower levels at this site
post_text: The oldest known elongated skulls in China date to approximately 12,000 years ago, not 10,000. The site name "Dàrén Cùyū (Darren Cuyu)" does not correspond to any verified archaeological site in available records, and the elongated skulls from this period are not associated with Dawenkou culture, which dates to roughly 4,300–2,600 BCE. Claims about excavation methodology causing later artifacts to appear in lower strata remain unverified.

Host notes the site's top level was excavated first, meaning all archaeologists have passed through the oldest strata

Host argues this discovery pattern reflects excavation order, not chronological anomalies
